root_idea.summary: The root centers on a grimacing, stern, or distorted expression of the face, especially with the lips drawn back and the teeth exposed.
root_idea.development: Classical extensions include the mouth and surrounding parts, severe or barren times, and derived or figurative uses involving causing the expression, smiling, lightning, and affliction.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular active-participle citation form كَالِحٌ rather than the Quran-only plural surface form.

senses.definition: Having the lips drawn back from the teeth, grimacing with a stern, morose, or frowning expression.
senses.usage_conditions: Quranic active-participle use describing faces marked by this distorted expression; the expression involves displaying or exposing the teeth rather than a neutral facial posture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To frighten someone by grimacing in his face.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A construction with فِي وَجْهِهِ, expressing the frightening effect of the grimace.
Form II usage, especially with the face as object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Contending with someone for superiority in strength.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun describing a contest of strength.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone grin or display the teeth while frowning or contracting the face.

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended or figurative Form V usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of lightning, to flash in continued succession; also to continue and become concealed in a white cloud.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative usage applied to lightning and its intermittent concealment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The mouth and the parts surrounding it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical noun referring to the mouth region.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A year of dearth, scarcity, drought, sterility, or barrenness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions for a barren or impoverished year.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Severe, distressing, or afflictive, of fortune or time.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the construction دَهْرٌ كَالِحٌ and related descriptions of harsh circumstances.
An epithet applied to a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A trial or affliction whose severity makes people grin and frown.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective describing a severe ordeal or affliction.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The basic grimacing and tooth-displaying action is covered by the Quranic participial sense.
Pointer-only cross-reference to the basic entry.
Grammatical identification as the active participle of the basic verb.
Severe or distressing fortune or time.

cautions: Lane's printed Quran reference for the participial use is reported as “Kur xxiii. 106” in the evidence; it is not treated as a modern verse location. The Quran example here uses the independently supplied QAC occurrence at 23:104:6.
